# API Documentation

**Status: implemented in Phase 3.** The API runs locally through Docker Compose and has not been deployed. Interactive documentation is generated by FastAPI at `/docs`, and the machine-readable schema at `/openapi.json`.

> **How to read a score.** `model_score` ranks transactions for review. It is **not calibrated** and is **not a probability of fraud**. `FLAG_FOR_REVIEW` asks a person to look, and is not a finding of fraud. On the test partition, the frozen threshold flagged 45.9% of labelled fraud (21.9% in normal steps), 40.7% of flags were labelled fraud, and the false positive rate was 0.282% against a 0.1% target. Every prediction response carries `score_is_calibrated: false`.

## Base address and authentication

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Local address | `http://127.0.0.1:${API_HOST_PORT}`, which is 8010 on the development computer |
| Web application | Cookie session: `POST /api/v1/auth/session` with JSON `{email, password}` sets HttpOnly cookies. Requests that change data also need `X-CSRF-Token` and an allowed `Origin`. |
| API clients and Swagger | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, form fields `username` (the email) and `password`. No CSRF token needed. |
| Public routes | `/health`, `/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json`, `/api/v1/auth/login` and `/api/v1/auth/session` |
| Lifetime | 30 minutes for both, then sign in again |
| First account | `scripts/create_admin.py`, since there is no self-registration |

Credentials prove identity only. The role is read from the database on each request, so deactivating an account or changing a role applies immediately. Changing a password ends every session and token.

### Browser sessions

| Cookie | Flags | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `finguard_session` | HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/api, Secure in production | Signed token naming a server-side session |
| `finguard_csrf` | SameSite=Strict, Path=/, Secure in production, readable by page script | Value to send as `X-CSRF-Token` on POST, PATCH and DELETE |

`DELETE /api/v1/auth/session` signs out, revoking that session only. The web application calls `/api` on its own origin, through a proxy, so the cookies stay first-party (ADR 0004).

## Roles

| Action | Demo | Analyst | Investigator | Admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Predict, upload CSV, explore transactions, read models, summary, settings, status | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| View investigations, export reports | | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Update investigations, add notes | | | Yes | Yes |
| Change settings, manage users, read the audit log | | | | Yes |

Demo users see only records they or other demo users created, all marked `is_demo: true`, and everyone else sees only non-demo records. Demo records never open an investigation.

## Endpoints

PRD 8.2 endpoints, plus additions marked with an asterisk.

| Method and path | Permission | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | none | Liveness only: `{"status": "ok"}` |
| `GET /api/v1/system/status` | any role | Database and model state, model hash and threshold |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/login` * | none | Get a token |
| `POST`, `DELETE /api/v1/auth/session` * | none | Browser sign-in and sign-out |
| `GET /api/v1/auth/me` * | any role | Your account, permissions and session expiry |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/change-password` * | any role | Change your password, signing out other sessions |
| `GET`, `POST /api/v1/users`, `PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}` * | admin | Manage accounts. An administrator cannot deactivate their own account (422), and the last active administrator cannot be demoted (422). |
| `GET /api/v1/users/assignable` * | investigator, admin | Active investigators and admins: id, email and role only |
| `GET /api/v1/audit-logs` * | admin | Audit log, newest first |
| `POST /api/v1/transactions/predict` | any role | Score one transaction |
| `GET /api/v1/transactions` | any role | Explorer with filters, sorting and paging |
| `GET /api/v1/transactions/{transaction_id}` | any role | Detail, with explanation and investigation |
| `POST /api/v1/batches/upload` | any role | Upload a CSV, processed in the background |
| `GET /api/v1/batches` * | any role | Your scope's batch jobs |
| `GET /api/v1/batches/{batch_id}` | any role | Status and progress |
| `GET /api/v1/batches/{batch_id}/results` | any role | Stored results, paged |
| `GET /api/v1/batches/{batch_id}/export` | any role | Results as CSV |
| `GET /api/v1/batches/{batch_id}/errors` * | any role | Row error report as CSV |
| `GET /api/v1/investigations` | analyst and above | Queue, filter by `investigation_status` or `assigned_user_id` |
| `GET /api/v1/investigations/{investigation_id}` * | analyst and above | Notes and status history |
| `PATCH /api/v1/investigations/{investigation_id}` | investigator, admin | Change status or assignee |
| `POST /api/v1/investigations/{investigation_id}/notes` | investigator, admin | Add a note |
| `GET /api/v1/models` | any role | Registered versions |
| `GET /api/v1/models/active` | any role | The model in use |
| `GET /api/v1/models/metrics` | any role | Frozen Phase 2 evaluation, with `performance_notes` |
| `GET /api/v1/models/feature-importance` | any role | Saved SHAP importance and its limits |
| `GET /api/v1/models/report` * | any role | Saved comparison, curves, thresholds and experiment history, from `model_v1_report.json` |
| `GET /api/v1/reports/summary` | any role | Totals for your scope |
| `GET /api/v1/reports/export?report_type=` | analyst and above | `predictions`, `flag_summary`, `investigations` or `model_evaluation` as CSV |
| `GET`, `PATCH /api/v1/settings` | read: any role. change: admin | Settings, versions, dataset and health |

Every JSON route declares request and response schemas. Routes returning CSV are documented as `text/csv`. A test walks `/openapi.json` and confirms that every route except the public ones refuses requests without a token.

## Predicting one transaction

`POST /api/v1/transactions/predict`

```json
{
  "external_transaction_id": "ABC-1",
  "amount": 9000000.00,
  "transaction_type": "TRANSFER",
  "step": 5,
  "destination_category": "customer"
}
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `external_transaction_id` | Optional. 1 to 64 characters, letters, digits and `_ . : -`, starting with a letter or digit. Generated as `TXN-...` if omitted. Must be unique, otherwise 409. |
| `amount` | Above 0, at most 2 decimal places, finite |
| `transaction_type` | `CASH_IN`, `CASH_OUT`, `DEBIT`, `PAYMENT` or `TRANSFER` |
| `step` | Integer from 1 to 1,000,000. Only `step % 24`, the simulated hour, reaches the model. |
| `destination_category` | `customer` or `merchant`. `merchant` only with `PAYMENT`, and `PAYMENT` only with `merchant`, since PaySim has no other combination. |

Any other field, including `isFraud` or a balance, gives 422.

Response, status 201, trimmed:

```json
{
  "model_score": 0.8377037048339844,
  "score_type": "uncalibrated_model_score",
  "score_is_calibrated": false,
  "score_note": "model_score ranks transactions for review. It is not a calibrated probability of fraud, ...",
  "risk_score": 83.77037048339844,
  "risk_level": "HIGH",
  "prediction": "FLAG_FOR_REVIEW",
  "model_version": "fraud_detector_v1",
  "threshold_used": 0.02841914258897305,
  "high_risk_boundary_used": 0.3,
  "investigation_status": "NEW",
  "explanation": {
    "method": "xgboost_tree_shap",
    "output_scale": "log_odds",
    "base_value": -6.9,
    "by_group": {"amount": 1.2, "hour": 2.1, "transaction_type_and_destination": 5.2},
    "by_feature": [{"feature": "transaction_type_TRANSFER", "contribution": 3.1}],
    "limitations": ["SHAP explains this model's output. It does not establish that a feature causes fraud.", "..."]
  }
}
```

The explanation values above are illustrative of the shape. The score is the real response measured end to end.

### Risk levels

| Level | Rule | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `LOW` | `model_score` below the frozen threshold, 0.02842 | `NOT_FLAGGED` |
| `MEDIUM` | At or above the threshold, below the high boundary | `FLAG_FOR_REVIEW` |
| `HIGH` | At or above the high boundary, 0.30 by default | `FLAG_FOR_REVIEW` |

The threshold cannot be changed through the API. Administrators can move the high boundary, which changes only the Medium and High labels of future predictions. `risk_score` is `model_score * 100`, and is not a percentage chance.

## Explorer

`GET /api/v1/transactions` accepts `external_id` (contains, case-insensitive), `risk_level`, `prediction`, `transaction_type`, `amount_min`, `amount_max`, `step_min`, `step_max`, `investigation_status`, `batch_job_id`, `sort_by` (`created_at`, `amount`, `model_score` or `step`), `sort_order`, `limit` (1 to 200) and `offset`. It returns `{items, total, limit, offset}`.

## CSV upload

`POST /api/v1/batches/upload`, multipart field `file`.

| Rule | Limit or behaviour |
|---|---|
| Extension | `.csv` only |
| Size | 10 MB (`MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`). Larger requests are refused before the body is read. |
| Rows | 50,000 (`MAX_BATCH_ROWS`) |
| Encoding | UTF-8, with or without a byte-order mark |
| Required columns | `amount`, `transaction_type`, `step`, `destination_category` |
| Optional | `external_transaction_id` |
| Ignored and reported | `isFraud`, `isFlaggedFraud`. `isFraud` values of 0 or 1 are kept in a separate table and never reach the model. |
| Refused | Balance and account columns, and any unknown column |

The response is 202 with a `BatchView`. Processing continues in the background in chunks of 1,000 rows. Poll `GET /batches/{id}` for `processed_records`, `failed_records`, `succeeded_records` and `progress_percent`. Bad rows do not stop good ones. The error report lists row number, column and reason, without the rejected value. Status ends as `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS` or `FAILED`. A job interrupted by a restart is marked `FAILED` at the next start-up and must be uploaded again.

## Errors

Every error is JSON with `detail` and `request_id`. Validation errors also carry `errors`, listing location, message and type, without the submitted value.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 401 | Missing, invalid or outdated token, or wrong credentials |
| 403 | Your role does not allow this, or a cookie request lacked a valid CSRF token or allowed origin |
| 404 | Not found, or outside your demo scope |
| 409 | The identifier already exists |
| 413 | Upload too large, or too many rows |
| 422 | Invalid input |
| 429 | Rate limited, with `Retry-After`. Login: 5 failures per minute per address and email. Predict: 120 per minute. Upload: 10 per minute. |
| 500 | "Internal server error." Details are logged on the server only. |

## Model metrics

`GET /api/v1/models/metrics` serves the saved file `artifacts/metadata/model_v1_metrics.json` unchanged, with validation and test results at the frozen threshold, results by sparse and normal steps, and `performance_notes` built from those values:

- The false positive rate on test was 0.282%, 2.8 times the 0.1% target set on validation. The target was not met.
- Recall on test was 45.9% overall, so 54.1% of labelled fraud was not flagged.
- Recall was 21.9% in normal steps and 56.1% in sparse steps.
- Precision was 40.7%, so most flags were not labelled fraud.
- Test's higher fraud rate (0.420% against 0.059% on validation) explains part of its higher precision.

No metric is recalculated, and the test partition is not read.

## Model report

`GET /api/v1/models/report` serves `artifacts/metadata/model_v1_report.json` unchanged. `scripts/export_model_report.py` built that file by copying values from six saved Phase 2 files, whose hashes it records. No data partition was read and nothing was recalculated. The API checks the file against a hash pinned in code at start-up. It holds:

- the family comparison, with intervals and timings;
- validation curves for every family, and validation and test curves for the selected model;
- confusion matrices and the threshold analysis;
- the imbalance matrix and all 125 recorded runs;
- the LightGBM diagnostic, and the statements the interface must show.

## Security headers

JSON responses carry `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `/docs` and `/redoc` get a separate policy allowing the CDN and inline script they need. Forwarded client addresses are believed only from proxies listed in `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS`, which is empty by default.
